assignment.title: Algebra II Honors — Operations on Polynomials

questions.prompt: Getting ready — multiplying monomials. To multiply monomials, multiply the coefficients and add the exponents of the same letter: $x^{a} \cdot x^{b} = x^{a+b}$. Write each product in simplest form.
hints: Multiply the coefficients first, and watch the sign: a positive times a negative is negative.
For the same letter, add the exponents: x² · x⁵ has 2 + 5 factors of x.
In the second product, a letter written with no exponent has exponent 1: a³ · a = a⁴.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. x² · x⁵ is x multiplied by itself…

questions.prompt: Getting ready — the opposite of a polynomial, and like terms. A minus sign in front of parentheses changes the sign of EVERY term inside. Like terms have the same letter raised to the same exponent; combine them by adding their coefficients. Write each answer in simplest form.
hints: The minus sign in front means −1 times every term: −1 · a³, −1 · (−3a), and −1 · 2.
Only like terms combine: the a² terms with each other, and the a terms with each other.
Add the coefficients of like terms and keep the letter and exponent: 4a² − a² has coefficient 4 − 1.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. The opposite of −3a is…

questions.prompt: Getting ready — like terms. Each box shows two terms. Are they like terms? If they are not, say why.

responses.label: 3x²y and −5yx²
options: Like terms — same letters, same exponents
Not like terms — the exponents are different
Not like terms — the letters are different
responses.answer: Like terms — same letters, same exponents

responses.label: 4a³ and 4a²
options: Not like terms — the exponents are different
Not like terms — the letters are different
Like terms — same letters, same exponents
responses.answer: Not like terms — the exponents are different

responses.label: 6m² and 6n²
options: Not like terms — the letters are different
Like terms — same letters, same exponents
Not like terms — the exponents are different
responses.answer: Not like terms — the letters are different

hints: Like terms have exactly the same letters, each raised to the same exponent. The coefficients do not matter.
The order the letters are written in does not matter: yx² is the same as x²y.
Same coefficient is not enough: check the exponents, then check the letters.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. Two terms are like terms when they have…
options: the same letters with the same exponents
scaffold.correct: the same letters with the same exponents

sections.title: Classwork — Add, Subtract and Multiply Polynomials

questions.prompt: New vocabulary. Sort each expression: is it a monomial, a binomial, a trinomial — or not a polynomial at all?
hints: Count the terms: the parts joined by + or −. One term is a monomial, two a binomial, three a trinomial.
A product such as 5xy or −4x²y³ is ONE term, however many letters it has.
Check for a variable under a radical or in a denominator first: then it is not a polynomial at all.

steps.title: Monomial
steps.instruction: A monomial is a number, a variable, or the product of a number and one or more variables: 5, y, 5xy, −4x²y³.

steps.title: Binomial
steps.instruction: A binomial is the sum of two monomials: 5 + z, x² − 4y, r⁶t⁷ + r⁴t⁸.

steps.title: Trinomial
steps.instruction: A trinomial is the sum of three monomials: 2x + 3y + 4z, x² − 3x + 40.

steps.title: Not a polynomial
steps.instruction: A polynomial never has a variable in a denominator or under a radical: x² + √x and (ab³ − 1)/(az⁴ + 3) are not polynomials.

questions.prompt: The degree of a monomial is the sum of the exponents of its variables. The degree of a polynomial is the greatest degree of any of its terms. Give the degree of each.
hints: A letter with no exponent written has exponent 1, so 5xy has exponents 1 and 1.
For one term, ADD the exponents of all its letters.
For a polynomial, find each term's degree and take the greatest.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. The degree of the monomial −4x²y³ is…

steps.title: Degree of a monomial
steps.instruction: The sum of the exponents of its variables. A nonzero number alone has degree 0.

steps.title: Degree of a polynomial
steps.instruction: The greatest degree of any of its terms.

steps.title: Simplify
steps.instruction: A polynomial is simplified when it has no parentheses, every product is multiplied out, and no two terms are like terms.

questions.prompt: Example A. Simplify $(2a^3 + 5a - 7) - (a^3 - 3a + 2)$. Subtracting a polynomial means adding its opposite: write the opposite of every term of the second polynomial, then combine like terms column by column.
hints: The minus sign in front of (a³ − 3a + 2) changes the sign of EVERY term inside — not just the first.
The opposite of −3a is +3a, and the opposite of +2 is −2.
In each column, add the coefficients: the a column holds 5a and the opposite of −3a.

steps.title: Distribute the −1
steps.instruction: (2a³ + 5a − 7) − (a³ − 3a + 2) = 2a³ + 5a − 7 − a³ + 3a − 2: every sign in the second polynomial changes.

steps.title: Combine like terms
steps.instruction: Add the coefficients in each group to write the answer in simplest form.

questions.prompt: Example B. Simplify $(4x^2 - 9x + 3) + (-2x^2 - 5x - 6)$. Align like terms vertically and add.
hints: Each column holds one kind of term: the x² terms, the x terms, and the constants.
Add the coefficients in each column and keep the letter and exponent.
Watch the signs: −9x + (−5x) is −14x.

questions.prompt: Check Your Progress. Now without the workshop: simplify each difference. Write each answer in simplest form.
hints: First rewrite each subtraction as adding the opposite of EVERY term in the second polynomial.
The opposite of 4x² + x − 5 is −4x² − x + 5.
Then combine the x² terms, the x terms and the constants.

questions.prompt: Error analysis. Jordan simplified $(5y^2 - 2y + 4) - (2y^2 - 6y + 1)$ and wrote: $5y^2 - 2y + 4 - 2y^2 - 6y + 1 = 3y^2 - 8y + 5$.

responses.label: What did Jordan do wrong?
options: He changed the sign of only the first term of the second polynomial.
He subtracted the first polynomial from the second.
responses.answer: He changed the sign of only the first term of the second polynomial.

responses.label: The correct difference in simplest form

hints: Compare Jordan's second step with the second polynomial: which signs changed, and which did not?
Subtracting (2y² − 6y + 1) adds −2y² + 6y − 1.
Now combine like terms: 5y² − 2y², −2y + 6y, and 4 − 1.

questions.prompt: Example: Simplify by using the Distributive Property. Find $-y(4y^2 + 2y - 3)$. The area model has one row, $-y$, and one column for each term of $4y^2 + 2y - 3$: fill in every cell, then write the product.
hints: Each cell is −y times the term at the top of its column.
Multiply the coefficients (watch the signs) and add the exponents of y: −y · 4y² = −4y³.
No two cells are like terms here, so the product is the three cells added together.

steps.title: Distributive Property
steps.instruction: a(b + c + d) = ab + ac + ad: the monomial outside multiplies EVERY term inside.

steps.title: Multiply the monomials
steps.instruction: Multiply the coefficients and add the exponents of the same letter: −y(4y²) = −4y³.

questions.prompt: Check Your Progress. Distribute and simplify. Write each answer in simplest form.
hints: The monomial outside multiplies every term inside, and its sign goes with it.
Add the exponents of the same letter: 3x² · 2xy = 6x³y.
Leave unlike terms separate: x³y and x³y² are not like terms.

questions.prompt: E-SALES. A small online retailer estimates that the cost, in dollars, of selling x units of a product is C(x) = 0.001x² + 5x + 500, and the revenue from selling x units is R(x) = 10x. Profit is revenue minus cost.

responses.label: Which expression is the profit P(x) = R(x) − C(x)?
The profit P(x) in simplest form
The profit, in dollars, when 1000 units are sold

hints: The whole cost is subtracted, so it goes in parentheses: every term of the cost changes sign.
Combine the x terms: 10x − 5x.
Substitute x = 1000 into your simplified polynomial: −0.001(1000)² + 5(1000) − 500.

steps.title: Why simplify?
steps.instruction: A simplified polynomial is quicker to evaluate and to compare: one x term instead of two.

questions.prompt: Example: Multiply polynomials. Find $(a^2 + 3a - 4)(a + 2)$. The area model has a row for each term of $a^2 + 3a - 4$ and a column for each term of $a + 2$.
hints: Every term of the first polynomial multiplies every term of the second: 3 rows × 2 columns is 6 products.
In each cell, multiply the coefficients and add the exponents: a² · a = a³, 3a · 2 = 6a.
Cells with the same power of a are like terms: 2a² and 3a² combine, and so do 6a and −4a.

steps.title: Distribute every term
steps.instruction: (a² + 3a − 4)(a + 2) = a²(a + 2) + 3a(a + 2) − 4(a + 2): each term of the first polynomial multiplies the whole second polynomial.

steps.title: Multiply the monomials
steps.instruction: a³ + 2a² + 3a² + 6a − 4a − 8 — the six cells of the area model.

steps.title: Combine like terms
steps.instruction: Add the like terms to write the product in simplest form.

questions.prompt: Check Your Progress. Find $(x^2 + 3x - 2)(x + 4)$ without the area model.

responses.label: How many products do you find before combining like terms?

hints: Each of the 3 terms of the first polynomial multiplies each of the 2 terms of the second.
The products are x³, 4x², 3x², 12x, −2x, −8.
Combine the x² terms and the x terms.

scaffold.prompt: Let’s back up. Multiplying a trinomial by a binomial makes…

questions.prompt: Simplify each difference. Write each answer in simplest form.
hints: Change the sign of every term of the polynomial you subtract.
In the second difference there is no b term to subtract: 6b stays as it is.
Combine the like terms in each difference.

questions.prompt: Simplify $4(a^2 + 5a - 6) - 3(2a^3 + 4a - 5)$. Write the answer in simplest form.
hints: Distribute 4 to every term of the first polynomial and −3 to every term of the second.
Write the like terms together, highest power first, and combine.

questions.prompt: Multiply. Write each product in simplest form.
hints: Multiply every term of one factor by every term of the other.
In (n − 9)(n + 7) the two n terms are like terms: 7n − 9n.
3p · np = 3np²: the two factors of p multiply to p².

questions.prompt: Simplify $5c(2c^2 - 3c + 4) + 2c(7c - 8)$. Write the answer in simplest form.
hints: Distribute 5c to all three terms of the first polynomial, and 2c to both terms of the second.
Combine the c² terms and the c terms.

questions.prompt: TEKS review. Which expression is equivalent to $(2y^3 - 5y^2 - 4) - (4y^3 + 11y^2 - 3y + 5)$?

responses.label: Which mistake gives −2y³ + 6y² − 3y + 1?
options: Subtracting only the first term of the second polynomial
Adding the polynomials, then taking the opposite of the sum
Subtracting the first polynomial from the second
responses.answer: Subtracting only the first term of the second polynomial

responses.label: Add the expressions −2y³ − 16y² + 3y − 9 and 2y³ + 16y² − 3y + 9. Their sum is

hints: Change the sign of every term of 4y³ + 11y² − 3y + 5 before you combine.
Try the mistake: subtract only 4y³ and leave the other terms of the second polynomial as they are. Which choice do you get?
P − Q and Q − P are opposites, so what is their sum?

questions.prompt: TEKS review. Sammy and Luis each threw a ball into the air at the same time. The height, in feet, of Sammy's ball after t seconds is $2 + 40t - 16t^2$, and the height of Luis's ball is $2 + 35t - 16t^2$. Subtract to find how much higher Sammy's ball is than Luis's after t seconds.
hints: Write the opposite of every term of Luis's height.
The t² column and the constant column cancel: type 0 for a column whose terms add to 0.
What is left tells you how the gap between the balls grows each second.

questions.prompt: TEKS review. Find $(m^2 - m + 1)(m + 1)$.
hints: Fill in all six cells: each term of m² − m + 1 times m, then times 1.
Look for like terms that cancel: m² and −m², −m and m.
A product can have fewer terms than you expect when like terms cancel.

questions.prompt: PAINTING. Connor hired two painters. The first charges $12 per hour and the second charges $11 per hour. The job takes 15 hours of labor in all. Write each answer in simplest form.

responses.label: Total cost if the first painter works x of the 15 hours
Total cost if the second painter works y of the 15 hours

hints: If the first painter works x hours, the second works the rest: 15 − x hours.
Cost = 12x + 11(15 − x). Distribute, then combine like terms.
For the second answer the second painter works y hours and the first works 15 − y.

questions.prompt: INTEREST. Olivia has $1300 to invest in a government bond that pays 2.2% per year and a savings account that pays 1.9% per year. She invests x dollars in the bond and the rest in savings.

responses.label: The interest she earns in one year, in simplest form
The interest, in dollars, if she invests $800 in the bond

hints: The rest of the money is 1300 − x dollars.
Interest = 0.022x + 0.019(1300 − x). Distribute the 0.019.
Combine the x terms: 0.022x − 0.019x.

questions.prompt: APPLY MATH. The number of bachelor's degrees, in thousands, earned by males and by females x years after 1971 is about $0.108x^2 - 0.876x + 474.1$ and $0.047x^2 + 9.694x + 361.7$. Write each answer in simplest form.

responses.label: Degrees earned by men and women together
How many more degrees men earned than women (men − women)

hints: For the total, add like terms: 0.108x² + 0.047x², and so on.
For the difference, subtract EVERY term of the women's polynomial.

questions.prompt: Honors. Find $(x - y)(x^2 + 2xy + y^2)$. Two letters: a cell's letters are the letters of its row and column together.
hints: Each cell multiplies a row term by a column term: x · 2xy = 2x²y.
Like terms need the same letters with the same exponents: 2x²y and −x²y combine; x²y and xy² do not.
Two pairs of cells combine. The product has four terms.

questions.prompt: Honors. Find $(4n - 5)^3$ in two steps: square $4n - 5$, then multiply the result by $4n - 5$ again. Write each answer in simplest form.
hints: (4n − 5)² = (4n − 5)(4n − 5): four products, and the two middle ones are like terms.
Now multiply your trinomial by 4n − 5: six products.
Combine the like terms: two n² terms and two n terms.

questions.prompt: TEKS review. The volume of a rectangular prism is the product of its length, width and height. Adriana's box has length $7p$, width $3p - 4$ and height $2p^2$ units.

responses.label: Which expression is the volume in cubic units?
The volume, in cubic units, when p = 2

hints: Multiply all three: 7p(3p − 4)(2p²).
7p(3p − 4) = 21p² − 28p; then multiply each term by 2p².
Substitute p = 2 into your product.

questions.prompt: [College-Readiness — SAT style] Answer each question.

responses.label: If (2x + k)(x − 3) = 2x² + x − 21 for all values of x, what is the value of k?
The expression (3x² − 5x + 2) − (x² − 2x − 4) is equivalent to ax² + bx + c. What is a + b + c?

hints: Multiply out (2x + k)(x − 3) and match the coefficients of x with 2x² + x − 21.
The x coefficient of the product is −6 + k.
Simplify the difference first; then add the three coefficients.

questions.prompt: Honors — always, sometimes or never? Sort each statement. For "sometimes", you should be able to find an example where it is true and one where it is false.

figures.text: The product of two monomials is a monomial.
The difference of two polynomials is a polynomial.
Subtracting a polynomial from itself gives 0.
The sum of two binomials is a binomial.
A binomial times a trinomial has 6 terms after like terms are combined.
The sum of two polynomials of degree 3 has degree 3.
A monomial has a variable in a denominator.
Multiplying two binomials in x, each of degree 1, gives a polynomial of degree 3.

hints: Test each statement with examples. One counterexample is enough to rule out "always".
(x + 1)(x² − x + 1) = x³ + 1: like terms can cancel.
x³ + (−x³ + x) = x: the highest-degree terms can cancel when you add.

questions.prompt: Subtract $(5x^3 - 2x^2 + 7) - (2x^3 + 4x^2 - 3x + 1)$. Write the opposite of every term you subtract, combine each column of like terms, and write the result in simplest form.
Multiply $(2x^2 - 3x + 4)(x - 5)$. Fill in every cell of the area model, then write the product in simplest form.
A company's cost to make x items is C(x) = 0.002x² + 4x + 350 dollars, and its revenue from selling them is R(x) = 12x dollars. Profit is revenue minus cost.

responses.label: Which expression is the profit P(x) = R(x) − C(x)?
The profit P(x) in simplest form
The profit, in dollars, when 500 items are sold
